explanation: Compared against Problem 33 of Ben Green's '100 open problems' (p. 18): 'Are there infinitely many q for which there is a set A ⊂ Z/qZ, |A| = (√2 + o(1))q^{1/2}, with A + A = Z/qZ?' The statement says that for every ε > 0 there are infinitely many q (ℕ+, atTop) with some A ⊆ ZMod q satisfying A + A = ZMod q and | |A|/√q - √2 | < ε. By a diagonal argument this is equivalent to a sequence q_j → ∞ with sets A_j, A_j + A_j = Z/q_jZ and |A_j| = (√2 + o(1))√q_j, the intended meaning. (Values of |A| below (√2 - ε)√q are impossible for large q, since |A + A| <= |A|(|A| + 1)/2.) Faithful; open.
